## TL;DR  

*The shield layers that come with the standard **OpenMapTiles-based OSM styles** (OSM Bright, OSM Liberty, etc.) look for sprite IDs that are built from the **network name** (`us-interstate`, `us-highway`, `us-state` or the generic `road`) plus an underscore and the **ref-length** (`_1 … _6`).*  

| Network (value of the `network` property) | Sprite ID pattern | Example for a 2-digit ref |
|-------------------------------------------|-------------------|---------------------------|
| `us-interstate` (I-xx)                    | `us-interstate_<len>` | `us-interstate_2` |
| `us-highway`   (US-xx)                    | `us-highway_<len>`    | `us-highway_3` |
| `us-state`     (CA-xx, TX-xx, …)         | `us-state_<len>`      | `us-state_2` |
| any other network (e.g. `road`)          | `road_<len>`          | `road_4` |

*If those IDs are missing from the style’s sprite sheet you will see only the numeric label (the `text-field` part of the shield layer) – the “bare floating numbers” you described.*

The fix is **simply to use a sprite sheet that contains those IDs**. You do **not** have to edit any layer definitions.

Below is a step-by-step guide that tells you exactly which IDs you need, where to get a ready-made sprite that already contains them, and how to add the missing images yourself if you prefer a custom sprite.

---

## 1. What the style actually asks for

### 1.1. The expression used in the style

Both OSM Bright and OSM Liberty define the shield layers roughly like this (the real style uses a few more properties, but the important part is the `icon-image` expression):

```json
{
  "id": "highway-shield-us-interstate",
  "type": "symbol",
  "source": "openmaptiles",
  "source-layer": "transportation_name",
  "layout": {
    "icon-image": "{network}_{ref_length}",
    "text-field": "{ref}",
    "symbol-placement": {
      "base": 1,
      "stops": [
        [7, "point"],
        [7, "line"],
        [8, "line"]
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

* `network` – a string that comes from the tile data (`us-interstate`, `us-highway`, `us-state`, or any other value).  
* `ref_length` – the length of the `ref` string (1-6).  
* The concatenated string is **the exact sprite ID** that MapLibre will look up.

### 1.2. The concrete IDs you must have

| `network` value | `ref_length` = 1 | `ref_length` = 2 | `ref_length` = 3 | `ref_length` = 4 | `ref_length` = 5 | `ref_length` = 6 |
|-----------------|------------------|------------------|------------------|------------------|------------------|------------------|
| `us-interstate` | `us-interstate_1` | `us-interstate_2` | `us-interstate_3` | – | – | – |
| `us-highway`    | `us-highway_1`    | `us-highway_2`    | `us-highway_3`    | – | – | – |
| `us-state`      | `us-state_1`      | `us-state_2`      | `us-state_3`      | `us-state_4`      | `us-state_5`      | `us-state_6` |
| any other (e.g. `road`) | `road_1` | `road_2` | `road_3` | `road_4` | `road_5` | `road_6` |

*Only the IDs that actually exist in the sprite can be rendered.*  
If a particular `network`/`ref_length` combination is not present, the style falls back to drawing only the `text-field` (the number) and emits a console warning:

```
Image "us-interstate_2" could not be loaded
```

---

## 2. Getting a sprite that already contains those IDs

### 2.1. Use the official OSM Bright / OSM Liberty sprite

The **official OSM Bright** sprite (the one the demo style uses) contains **all** of the IDs listed above:

```
https://demotiles.maplibre.org/styles/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite
```

*The URL is *extension-less*; MapLibre will request the JSON and PNG automatically.*

If you are happy to pull the sprite from the public CDN, just set (or replace) the `sprite` property in your style JSON:

```json
{
  "sprite": "https://demotiles.maplibre.org/styles/osm-bright-gl-style/sprite",
  ...
}
```

> **⚠️ Production note** – The demo CDN is fine for testing, but for a production site you should self-host the sprite (see 2.2).

### 2.2. Self-host the same sprite

1. **Download the sprite files** (PNG + JSON, plus the `@2x` variants) from the repo:

   *GitHub repo:* https://github.com/openmaptiles/osm-bright-gl-style/tree/master/sprite

   ```bash
   # Example using curl
   curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openmaptiles/osm-bright-gl-style/master/sprite/sprite.json
   curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openmaptiles/osm-bright-gl-style/master/sprite/sprite.png
   curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openmaptiles/osm-bright-gl-style/master/sprite/sprite@2x.json
   curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openmaptiles/osm-bright-gl-style/master/sprite/sprite@2x.png
   ```

2. **Put the four files on a static host** that you control (same origin as your style is ideal, otherwise make sure CORS headers allow cross-origin access).

3. **Point your style at the new base URL** (no extension):

   ```json
   {
     "sprite": "https://my.cdn.example.com/tiles/sprite"
   }
   ```

   The same base URL works for the normal and the `@2x` files; MapLibre will automatically request `sprite.json`, `sprite.png`, `sprite@2x.json`, `sprite@2x.png`.

### 2.3. Using the **multiple-sprite** feature (MapLibre GL JS ≥ 3.0)

If you already have a custom sprite for your own icons and you just want to *add* the OSM shield images, you can keep both sheets:

```json
{
  "sprite": [
    { "id": "default", "url": "https://my.cdn.example.com/my-icons/sprite" },
    { "id": "osm-shields", "url": "https://my.cdn.example.com/osm-bright/sprite" }
  ]
}
```

Then reference the shield images with the `id:` prefix **only if you need to** (the style itself already uses the default sheet, so you normally **don’t** have to change any `icon-image` values). The important part is that the sheet containing the shield IDs is loaded; the style will resolve `us-interstate_2` against the *default* sheet, which you have now made a composite of your own icons **plus** the OSM shield sheet.

---

If you cannot change the style’s `sprite` URL (e.g., you are using a third-party hosted style that you cannot edit) you can still supply the missing badge images with `Map.addImage()` after the map has loaded.

```js
map.on('load', async () => {
  // Helper to load a PNG from a URL and add it under the given id
  async function addBadge(id, url) {
    if (map.hasImage(id)) return;               // already present
    const { data } = await map.loadImage(url);   // PNG/WebP/JPEG only
    map.addImage(id, data, { sdf: false });      // ordinary bitmap
  }

  // List of badge IDs that the style may request (see table above)
  const badges = [
    // US Interstate (max 3 digits)
    'us-interstate_1', 'us-interstate_2', 'us-interstate_3',
    // US Highway
    'us-highway_1', 'us-highway_2', 'us-highway_3',
    // US State
    'us-state_1', 'us-state_2', 'us-state_3',
    'us-state_4', 'us-state_5', 'us-state_6',
    // Generic road (covers any other network)
    'road_1', 'road_2', 'road_3', 'road_4', 'road_5', 'road_6'
  ];

  // Base URL where you host the PNG badge files (you can copy them from the OSM Bright repo)
  const base = 'https://my.cdn.example.com/osm-shields/';

  await Promise.all(badges.map(id => addBadge(id, `${base}${id}.png`)));
});
```

* Where do you get the PNG files?  
  *The OSM Bright repo ships the PNGs in `sprite/sprite.png`. You can extract individual icons with any PNG-sprite-tool (e.g., `spritezero`, `png-sprite-extractor`, or even a quick script that reads the JSON index and cuts the PNG).*

* If you prefer **SVG** badges, you can rasterise them first (create a `<canvas>` or an `Image` element) and then call `addImage` with the resulting `HTMLImageElement`. Remember to set `crossOrigin = 'anonymous'` on the `Image` if the SVG is hosted on another domain.

* This approach works even with **MapLibre GL JS v6** – the `styleimagemissing` event will fire for each missing badge, and you can react to it:

```js
map.on('styleimagemissing', e => {
  const id = e.id;               // e.g., "us-interstate_2"
  // you could lazily load just the missing one here
});
```

| ✅ | Check | What to do if it fails |
|---|-------|------------------------|
| 1 | **Sprite URL is set** (`style.sprite`) and points to a *base* URL (no `.json`/`.png`). | Add the correct URL or self-host the sprite. |
| 2 | **Sprite JSON contains the needed IDs** (`us-interstate_2`, `us-highway_3`, …). | Use the official OSM Bright sprite, or merge those IDs into your own sprite, or add them with `addImage`. |
| 3 | **CORS is allowed** (the sprite files are served with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin:*` or your origin). | Adjust server headers or host on the same origin. |
| 4 | **Network & ref_length are present in the tile data** (you already confirmed this). | No action needed. |
| 5 | **No console “Image … could not be loaded” warnings** after fixing the sprite. | If warnings persist, double-check the exact ID spelling (including the underscore and length). |

When all three conditions (sprite URL, IDs present, CORS) are satisfied, the shield badge will appear automatically – no need to touch the layer definitions.

If you cannot change the style’s `sprite` property (e.g. you are using a third-party style that you cannot edit), you can register the missing images yourself after the map loads:

```js
map.on('load', async () => {
  // Helper to fetch a PNG and add it as an image
  async function addBadge(id, url) {
    if (map.hasImage(id)) return;               // already present
    const { data } = await map.loadImage(url);  // PNG, WebP, JPEG only
    map.addImage(id, data, { pixelRatio: 2 });   // match @2x if you have it
  }

  // List of badge URLs (you can host them yourself or copy from OSM Bright)
  const badges = [
    { id: 'us-interstate_1', url: 'https://mycdn.example.com/badges/us-interstate_1.png' },
    { id: 'us-interstate_2', url: 'https://mycdn.example.com/badges/us-interstate_2.png' },
    { id: 'us-interstate_3', url: 'https://mycdn.example.com/badges/us-interstate_3.png' },
    { id: 'us-highway_1',    url: 'https://mycdn.example.com/badges/us-highway_1.png' },
    { id: 'us-highway_2',    url: 'https://mycdn.example.com/badges/us-highway_2.png' },
    { id: 'us-highway_3',    url: 'https://mycdn.example.com/badges/us-highway_3.png' },
    { id: 'us-state_1',      url: 'https://mycdn.example.com/badges/us-state_1.png' },
    // … continue through us-state_6 and road_1-road_6
  ];

  for (const b of badges) await addBadge(b.id, b.url);
});
```

*Pros*: No need to touch the style JSON.  
*Cons*: Each badge is a separate HTTP request (unless you bundle them into a sprite and use `addSprite`).  

If you have many badges, prefer the **sprite** approach (3.1/3.2) because it loads a single PNG + JSON instead of dozens of individual files.

## 4. Quick checklist – “Why are my shields missing?”

| ✅ Check | What to do |
|--------|------------|
| **Sprite URL is correct** | Ensure `sprite` points to a base URL **without** `.json` or `.png`. |
| **Sprite loads (200 OK)** | Open `…/sprite.json` and `…/sprite.png` in the browser; they should return 200 and have CORS headers (`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` or your domain). |
| **Badge IDs exist in the JSON** | Open the JSON file and search for `us-interstate_2`, `road_4`, etc. |
| **`map.hasImage(id)` returns true** | Run the console snippet above for each ID. |
| **No CORS errors** | If the sprite is on another domain, it must send proper CORS headers; otherwise the browser will block the PNG. |
| **If you use multiple sprite sheets** | Remember to prefix IDs with the sheet’s `id` unless the sheet is `default`. |
| **If you added images at runtime** | Verify `map.loadImage` succeeded (no 404) and that you called `map.addImage` **after** the `load` event. |

If all the IDs from the table are present and `hasImage()` returns `true`, the shields will render automatically – no layer edits required.
